91220511.b:
About Ghasibah District in Diriyah

Ghasibah is one of the historic districts of Diriyah, which lies west of the Saudi capital, Riyadh. The district is notable for its heritage atmosphere and traditional buildings that reflect the history and rich culture of the area.

The district holds many archaeological landmarks from the period when it was a center of power and government in the First Saudi State. Ghasibah is also notable for its calm colors and unique architecture, making it a favorite destination for visitors who want to explore the history of the Kingdom.

Tourism in Ghasibah

Visiting historic and archaeological sites.

Exploring traditional markets and handicrafts.

Enjoying the natural scenery around the district.

The district also offers a range of cultural and social events that enhance the visitor experience and reflect the spirit of the local community. Ghasibah District is a symbol of Saudi heritage and an important part of the national identity.

91220489.b:
About Wadi Safar Dam

Wadi Safar Dam is one of the important dams in the Diriyah area of the capital, Riyadh, and is part of a water management project that aims to protect residential areas and farmland from floods and to strengthen water resources in the area. The dam is notable for its unique design and geography, which reflect the cultural and historical heritage of the area.

The dam extends along Wadi Safar and provides a suitable environment for storing rainwater during the winter, helping to distribute fresh water for crop irrigation and for residents' needs. It is also a tourist attraction for residents and visitors, who can enjoy the scenic nature and recreational activities around the dam.

With growing demand for water, Wadi Safar Dam is an example of the government's efforts in the Kingdom to secure water and improve the management of natural resources in support of sustainable development.

Wadi Safar Park is a wonderful natural destination in the Diriyah area, known for its beautiful scenery and varied terrain. The park is ideal for families and nature lovers, who can enjoy walking trails and strolls among local trees and plants.

The park also offers a range of recreational facilities, such as barbecue and seating areas, making it an ideal place to relax and spend time with friends and family. Visitors can also see the historic and cultural landmarks near the park, which adds to its appeal as an integrated tourist destination.

91220317.b:
About Jax District in Diriyah

Jax District is one of the modern districts of Diriyah in Saudi Arabia and a unique tourist and cultural destination. The district is notable for its contemporary architectural design, which harmonizes with the area's heritage and long history.

Jax District was established as a center for arts and culture, and includes many art galleries, restaurants and cafes offering unique experiences. The district also helps revive Saudi heritage through the cultural events and festivals held there.

Jax District is a meeting point for local and international visitors, who can enjoy an atmosphere full of creativity and the arts, making it an ideal destination for families and individuals alike.

Thanks to its strategic location near prominent historic landmarks, Jax District gives visitors the chance to explore Diriyah's rich heritage along with modern cultural experiences.
91220317.a: Jax District, Al Diriyah Al Jadidah, Diriyah

91218370.s: A window onto Riyadh's past and a scene from its long memory, embodied in the walls of the historic Murabba Palace, which stands on an area of 1,680 square meters, overflowing with the memory of the place, the historical events it witnessed, and the glory made on its soil.
91218370.b:
A window onto Riyadh's past and a scene from its long memory, embodied in the walls of the historic Murabba Palace, which stands on an area of 1,680 square meters, overflowing with the memory of the place, the historical events it witnessed, and the glory made on its soil.

The Story of Its Founding

By order of the late King Abdulaziz Al Saud, founder of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Murabba Palace was built two kilometers from old Riyadh, in step with the city's development and expansion at the time. The palace and its surroundings were established as a miniature city with several buildings. The King moved to live there in 1939 as a residence for himself and his family, a seat of government and state affairs, and a court where he received the leaders and heads of state of the world.

Authentic Architectural Heritage

On your visit to the historic Murabba Palace you will notice the distinctive design with an inner courtyard at the center of the palace, which all the rooms overlook. It was built in the manner prevalent at the time, conveying a unique architectural art. The surrounding environment left its mark on the palace's components: rooms and ceilings were covered with tamarisk trunks and decorated with palm fronds and leaves, the foundations were made of stone, and the walls of mud brick mixed with straw, decorated with patterns and ornaments printed on plaster. Despite the simplicity of the building, its beauty stands out in the zigzag columns supporting the palace's rooms and corridors.

Palace Layout and the King's Belongings

The palace is a square building surrounded by walls, reflecting the nature of the local community, which preserves the privacy of homes. It has 32 rooms on two floors, in addition to majlis halls for receiving the King's guests, and administrative offices for his aides and guards.

Enjoy discovering what the rooms hold on a historical tour inside the palace, including belongings, clothing, and commemorative photographs of the King with his sons and with a number of heads of state.

Visiting Hours

You can enjoy a journey into Riyadh's past with a visit to the historic Murabba Palace, open every day of the week at the following times: Saturday to Thursday, morning session 9 AM-12 PM and evening session 5 PM-8 PM; on Friday it can be visited during the evening session 5 PM-8 PM.
91218370.a: 2722 King Saud Rd, Al Murabba, Riyadh

90984623.s: Salwa Palace is an authentic icon of a glorious historical journey. The palace contains the Imam's residence and majlis, a school, supply storehouses and spaces for receiving guests. Today its striking architecture and towering walls bear witness to the political weight and depth of Saudi history.
90984623.b:
Salwa Palace is an authentic icon of a glorious historical journey. The palace contains the Imam's residence and majlis, a school, supply storehouses and spaces for receiving guests. Today its striking architecture and towering walls bear witness to the political weight and depth of Saudi history.

The ruling family moved from Ghasibah, the original seat of government, to the At-Turaif district, and in the time of Imam Abdulaziz bin Muhammad the foundation stone of Salwa Palace was laid. It became the second seat of government throughout the First Saudi State. Salwa Palace is distinguished by its high walls, vast spaces and architectural design, which stands as a witness to a history rich in glories.

90407257.s: Al Yanfa Village is one of the villages of the Tamniah center in the Asir region, in the south of Saudi Arabia, about 45 km from Abha. It contains a number of archaeological buildings, mosques and historic forts, showcases the architectural heritage of Asir, and is known for its mild climate and green nature.
90407257.b:
Al Yanfa Village is one of the villages of the Tamniah center in the Asir region, in the south of Saudi Arabia, about 45 km from Abha. It contains a number of archaeological buildings, mosques and historic forts, showcases the architectural heritage of Asir, and is known for its mild climate and green nature.

At an elevation of 2,600 meters above sea level and 40 kilometers southwest of Abha, Al Yanfa Archaeological Village, which dates back more than 1,400 years, is one of the oldest historic villages in the Asir region and one of the most unique in terms of architectural character and cultural identity.

The village has around 400 historic houses, 6 mosques and 36 old passageways linking the neighborhoods, along with striking stone terraces and farming areas fed by more than 70 wells, 7 of them carved into the rock.

Thanks to restoration work over the past two years, the village has become a vibrant center for contemporary arts, with its passageways and squares restored in natural stone, lighting inspired by heritage style installed, and a natural wooden system for draining rainwater.

At Al Yanfa Village, the charm of the place blends with the mild climate created by rain and seasonal winds, making the village a cultural and tourist destination that celebrates the beauty of the past and embraces the creativity of the present.

We are keen to strengthen the Kingdom's standing through products that blend the authenticity of our long heritage with a modern lifestyle, reflecting a true picture of the level of design and manufacturing quality in Saudi Arabia to its visitors around the world.

90071437.b:
When architecture meets haute couture.

In the heart of Al Bujairi in Diriyah, the Sit AlDar store unveils a unique collection titled "Where Architecture Meets Fashion", in which the spirit of Diriyah's historic architecture is embodied in designs that bring together fashion and creativity. The collection is inspired by the beauty of the old mud-brick houses and the rich heritage they carry. The store is in the heart of historic Diriyah, where every wall tells a story of resilience and legacy, so the store itself becomes an extension of this story, an immersive space where craftsmanship, heritage and innovation meet.

"Through this collection, Sit AlDar and Hassan bin Ghaith highlight the beauty of tradition with a contemporary touch, so that the art of the past is a lasting source of inspiration for the future. At the core of this project is a prestigious partnership between Sit AlDar and Hassan bin Ghaith, a distinguished name associated with traditional craftsmanship. This partnership is not merely a meeting of minds; it is a bridge between generations. Lubna Al Ghurair, with her contemporary vision for modern cultural expression, collaborates with Hassan bin Ghaith, guardian of textile heritage, to honor Saudi culture in an exceptional fusion of past and present."

90071289.s: The presence of two heritage wells near the farm ruins reflects an important aspect of Diriyah's agricultural legacy. The larger well is believed to have been used to irrigate the land, while the other served daily needs. These wells supplied water to the people of Samhan, showing the interconnection of local communities and their shared reliance on natural resources.
90071289.b:
The presence of two heritage wells near the farm ruins reflects an important aspect of Diriyah's agricultural legacy. The larger well is believed to have been used to irrigate the land, while the other served daily needs. These wells supplied water to the people of Samhan, showing the interconnection of local communities and their shared reliance on natural resources.

Today, Diriyah seeks to document this relationship and preserve it as part of the legacy of the water systems that supported agricultural life in the past.

90071240.s: The agricultural model in Al Suraiha draws its features from the old orchards of Wadi Hanifah, where people used to grow palms on three levels depending on the nature of the land. As rehabilitation work in the valley continues in the coming years, this traditional method will be revived through earthen irrigation channels and organic farming that suits the nature of the place.
90071240.b:
The agricultural model in Al Suraiha draws its features from the old orchards of Wadi Hanifah, where people used to grow palms on three levels depending on the nature of the land. As rehabilitation work in the valley continues in the coming years, this traditional method will be revived through earthen irrigation channels and organic farming that suits the nature of the place.

This approach aims to enhance biodiversity and soil health, and gives visitors the chance to experience a living picture of Diriyah's agricultural past.

90067656.s: The Al Suraiha district was distinguished by its fertility and a network of irrigation systems and wells that supported its agricultural nature, and it also supplied water to neighboring districts such as Samhan, whose residents fetched water daily. They filled jars and containers and carried them home on foot, on their shoulders or heads, or by donkey.
90067656.b:
The Al Suraiha district was distinguished by its fertility and a network of irrigation systems and wells that supported its agricultural nature, and it also supplied water to neighboring districts such as Samhan, whose residents fetched water daily. They filled jars and containers and carried them home on foot, on their shoulders or heads, or by donkey.

This communal activity highlights the importance of the link between the wells of Al Suraiha and the daily life of Samhan's residents. The skill of local craftsmen shows in the traditional stonework of the wells and the linear stone design of the water channels. Using traditional methods, conservation efforts continue to preserve these symbols of survival and community resilience in the face of a harsh climate.
